title: Meta warns that election backlash against data centers could make AI expansion harder
slides: Why is Meta suddenly worried about voters?
Election backlash now threatens data center expansion
Local opposition is blocking projects faster than regulators
Your region may see new siting rules within months
Check your local zoning agenda before the next vote
thread_text:
1. Meta's voter anxiety, explained

Meta is quietly funding election-integrity teams while its data center buildout faces something new: angry local voters, not federal regulators.

2. Backlash hits the grid

County boards are rejecting or delaying data center permits at record rates, citing water use and power bills — a bottleneck that bypasses Washington entirely.

3. Local vetoes outpace regulators

In at least a dozen states, planning commissions have blocked projects faster than utility regulators can approve them, according to industry tracking.

4. New rules are coming

Several states are drafting siting legislation that could land within months, giving local governments more say over where AI infrastructure goes.

5. Check your zoning agenda

Find your county planning calendar and see if a data center item is listed before the next vote. If it is, show up — or at least read the filing.
